newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukranian bank receives credit from Western banks.
newsitem.headline: Ukranian bank receives credit from Western banks.

text.p: One of Ukraine's three largest commercial banks on Thursday received a $16 million credit from a group of Western banks, the first time a Ukrainian bank has borrowed without government guarantees or trade obligations.
"There were no conditions or limits set on how we can use this money," Bank Ukraine's spokesman Viktor Fuklev said at a news conference about the six-month loan.

The Western banks were Austria's Raiffeisen Zentralbank Osterreich AG, the Netherlands' ING Bank NV, the Czech republic's Komercni Banka AS, and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Berliner Bank AG from Germany.
Switzerland's Finanz AG Zurich, a subsidiary of CS First Boston, Hungary's Magyar Kulkerskedelmi Bank RT and Poland's Kredyt Bank SA were also part of the group.
